verdict: Leads are coming in; Google spend needs its tracking fixed now.
narrative: In the last 28 days, Meta delivered all 138 leads at a cost of $15.76 per lead — a solid, stable result. Google Ads ran alongside it and spent $502.97 with zero conversions recorded, which traces to a broken conversion pixel rather than underperforming campaigns; that repair is underway. On the local presence side, Google Business Profile actions more than doubled week over week, driven by a rise in direction requests and calls. Leads are reaching the CRM but are not yet converting to booked appointments, which points to a gap in the intake process that is being addressed. Next period, expect conversion tracking on Google to come back online and the intake flow to begin turning inquiries into appointments.

highlights.phrase: leads received this period, all through Meta
cost per lead on Meta, holding steady
week-over-week rise in Google Business Profile actions

watch_item.issue: Google Ads spent $503 this period with no conversions recorded — the conversion pixel is not firing correctly, so results are being missed, not absent.
watch_item.fix: Conversion tracking is being repaired and offline conversion import is scheduled to go live by end of September, at which point Google campaigns will have accurate data to optimize against.
